newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uighur exiles say bombed bus in China.
newsitem.headline: Uighur exiles say bombed bus in China.

text.p: An exiled spokesman for Uighur nationalists in western China said on Tuesday his group had staged a bomb attack on a Chinese bus on Monday in reprisal for Beijing government measures against the Moslem ethnic group.

Mukhiddin Mukhlisi told Reuters in the nearby Kazakh capital Almaty he did not know how many victims there were in the attack, 120 km (75 miles) east of Yining in Xinjiang province. Chinese officials have said seven people died and over 60 were hurt in three previous bus bomb attacks in the region last week.
The explosion in the bus near the town of Kuldji (Yining) ...was our act of revenge for the crimes of the Chinese authorities," Mukhlisi, a prominent spokesman for the Uighur nationalist cause, said.

Accusing the Chinese police and army of killing 127 Uighurs and arresting hundreds more in an anti-separatist campaign which he said was launched last month, Mukhlisi added: "We intend to continue our struggle."
Last week's time bombs coincided with funeral rites for China's political patriarch Deng Xiaoping and were the latest example of brewing unrest in the oil-rich region.

Officially some nine million Uighurs live in China, mostly in Xinjiang, although Uighur nationalists striving for an independent homeland put the number at over 20 million. More than 300,000 Uighurs live in the former Soviet Union, to which many fled in the 1960s. About 180,000 have settled in Kazakhstan.
